opening_facts: A chain of 40 bike-repair shops kept revenue flat last year, but profit fell 18%. The number of repairs was also flat.
new_fact: Parts cost per repair is flat and mechanic pay per hour is unchanged, but the average repair now takes 65 minutes instead of 50 since the shops began servicing e-bikes.
model_answer_stage1: With revenue and repairs flat, profit likely fell because each repair costs more to do, most likely more mechanic time per job. I'd compare labor hours and parts cost per repair with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: parts and pay are flat, but each repair takes 30% longer, so labor cost per repair rose.

opening_facts: A sparkling-water brand launched a lemon flavor six months ago. It reached 60% of its first-month sales target, and sales have fallen 30% a month since.
new_fact: In stores that kept it in stock, repeat purchases matched the brand's other flavors. But 40% of stores ran out within two weeks and weren't restocked for a month.
model_answer_stage1: With sales falling 30% a month, shoppers who try lemon likely don't like it enough to buy it again. I'd compare repeat-purchase rates for lemon with the brand's other flavors.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: where lemon stayed in stock, repeat buying matched other flavors. The fall comes from stock-outs in 40% of stores.

opening_facts: Customers at a train-station car-rental branch now wait 25 minutes at the counter, up from 10 last year. Rentals are up 3%.
new_fact: Counter staff numbers are unchanged, but serving each customer now takes 9 minutes instead of 4 since a new ID-verification step was added.
model_answer_stage1: With rentals up only 3%, the longer waits more likely come from slower service per customer than from more customers. I'd compare time per customer at the counter with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: staffing is the same, but each customer takes 9 minutes instead of 4 since the new ID check.

opening_facts: A water park raised its day-ticket price 15% this summer. Ticket revenue fell 5%.
new_fact: Visits on hot weekends rose 2% at the new price, but visits on cool or rainy days fell 40%, and this summer had twice as many rainy days as last year.
model_answer_stage1: Revenue likely fell because the 15% price rise lost more visitors than it gained per ticket. I'd compare daily visits with last year, separating hot and rainy days.
model_answer_stage2: Revise: hot-weekend visits held at the higher price. The drop is on rainy days, and there were twice as many.

opening_facts: An online language-tutoring marketplace added 30% more tutors this year, but booked lessons grew only 5%.
new_fact: Student searches that ended without a booking rose from 10% to 25%, mostly searches for evening slots. Most new tutors offer only daytime hours.
model_answer_stage1: More tutors likely didn't help because they aren't available when students want lessons. I'd compare the time slots students search for with the slots tutors offer.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: failed searches rose to 25%, mostly for evenings, while new tutors teach in the daytime.

opening_facts: A food manufacturer's packaging costs rose 18% this year. Volume was flat, and packaging-material prices rose only 3%.
new_fact: The mix of pack sizes sold was unchanged, but packaging waste on the lines rose from 2% to 9% of material used after a new film supplier came in.
model_answer_stage1: With volume flat and prices up only 3%, the company is likely using more material per pack, probably through waste. I'd compare material used per pack with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: waste rose from 2% to 9% of material with the new film supplier, so each pack uses more film.

opening_facts: The service departments of a chain of 25 car dealerships lost 15% of their visits in a year, while car sales held steady.
new_fact: Warranty repair visits were flat. Visits for oil changes and tires fell 35% after two quick-service chains opened nearby, charging 30% less.
model_answer_stage1: With car sales steady, owners are likely taking routine work to cheaper or faster shops. I'd split lost visits by type of service and check where those owners now go.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: warranty visits held, but oil changes and tires fell 35% after cheaper quick-service chains opened.

opening_facts: Visits to a city's recreation centers fell 25% in two years, while the number of members rose 10%.
new_fact: Weekday-evening visits fell 50% after the centers cut evening hours to save on staff. Daytime and weekend visits are flat.
model_answer_stage1: With more members but fewer visits, members are likely finding it harder to come rather than losing interest, perhaps because of opening hours. I'd compare visits by time of day with two years ago.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: evening visits halved after evening hours were cut, while daytime and weekends held.

opening_facts: A concert venue's revenue per show fell 12% this year, while attendance held at 90% of capacity.
new_fact: The average ticket price is unchanged, but food and drink spending per guest fell 30% after the venue replaced its bars with app-only ordering.
model_answer_stage1: With attendance steady, revenue per show likely fell because guests spend less on food and drink, not on tickets. I'd compare bar sales per guest by month.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: ticket prices are unchanged, and food and drink spending per guest fell 30% after the switch to app-only ordering.

opening_facts: Late jobs at a commercial printer rose from 5% to 20% in three months. Order volume is flat.
new_fact: Press uptime and staffing are normal, but jobs now wait two days on average for customers to approve proofs since proofing moved from in person to an online portal.
model_answer_stage1: With volume flat, late jobs likely come from delays outside the presses, probably waiting for customer approvals. I'd measure how long each job spends at each step.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: presses and staff are normal, but jobs wait two days for proof approval since the online portal.

opening_facts: A meal-delivery app entered a new country a year ago and has 200,000 users. Only 15% have ordered more than once, against 45% in its home market.
new_fact: Users whose orders arrived within 30 minutes reordered at home-market rates. The average delivery time in the new country is 55 minutes because restaurants are spread out.
model_answer_stage1: Few users reorder, likely because the restaurant choice doesn't suit local tastes. I'd survey one-time users about why they didn't order again.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: users who got food in 30 minutes reordered like at home, so it's slow delivery, not the food.

opening_facts: A packaged-food company bought a snack brand last year, expecting 15% sales growth. The brand's sales have fallen 5% since the deal.
new_fact: Prices are unchanged. Sales held in the 3,000 stores where the brand kept its own sales team and fell 20% in the 2,000 stores moved to the buyer's sales force, which handles 300 other products.
model_answer_stage1: The brand likely lost attention after the deal, probably because the buyer's sales team has many other products to sell. I'd compare sales by store, by which team covers it.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: sales held where the brand's own team stayed and fell 20% where the buyer's busy sales force took over.

opening_facts: A wedding-dress shop's revenue fell 10% this year, while appointments rose 15%.
new_fact: The average dress price is unchanged. The share of appointments ending in a sale fell from 45% to 30%, mostly among appointments booked through a new free online booking page.
model_answer_stage1: More appointments but less revenue suggests the new appointments come from less serious shoppers, perhaps through easier booking. I'd compare sales rates by how each appointment was booked.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: fewer appointments end in a sale, mostly those from the free online booking page, at unchanged prices.

opening_facts: An ambulance service's average response time rose from 8 to 11 minutes this year. Calls rose 4%.
new_fact: Time from call to dispatch and driving times are unchanged, but ambulances now wait 40 minutes on average to hand patients over at hospitals, up from 15, so fewer are free.
model_answer_stage1: With calls up only 4%, slower responses more likely mean ambulances are busy longer on each call. I'd check how long each ambulance is tied up per call, step by step.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: handovers at hospitals now take 40 minutes instead of 15, so fewer ambulances are free.

opening_facts: A parking-garage operator raised downtown hourly rates 20%. Revenue rose only 2%.
new_fact: Daily and monthly parking revenue rose 18%, but short-stay hourly parkers fell 30% in the same month the city added cheaper street meters next door.
model_answer_stage1: Revenue rose only 2% on a 20% price rise, likely because hourly parkers are price-sensitive and many stopped using our garage at the higher rate. I'd compare hourly parkers before and after the change.
model_answer_stage2: Revise: hourly parkers fell 30%, but cheaper city meters opened next door the same month, so the cause is the meters.

opening_facts: A children's swim school grew enrollment 20% this year, but revenue grew only 4%.
new_fact: Prices and attendance per student are unchanged, but the share of students on the cheaper group-lesson plan rose from 40% to 75% after the school stopped offering private lessons on weekends.
model_answer_stage1: More students but slower revenue suggests students are shifting to cheaper lessons. I'd compare revenue per student by lesson type with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: prices held, and group lessons rose from 40% to 75% of students after weekend private lessons stopped.

opening_facts: A home-security alarm company's cancellations doubled in a year. Its prices haven't changed.
new_fact: Cancellations are concentrated among customers whose contracts ended this year. 60% of them say they switched to a $10-a-month do-it-yourself camera system, against the company's $45.
model_answer_stage1: Cancellations likely doubled because cheaper do-it-yourself systems now give customers an easy alternative. I'd ask cancelling customers what they switched to.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: 60% of cancelling customers moved to a $10 DIY system, against $45.

opening_facts: First-year dropout at a state's community colleges rose from 25% to 35% in two years, while enrollment rose 15%.
new_fact: Dropout rose only among students who enrolled through a new free-tuition program; it was flat for everyone else. Program students work 25 hours a week on average.
model_answer_stage1: With enrollment up 15%, the added students are likely less prepared for college work, so more leave. I'd compare first-year dropout for new and other students, by placement-test score.
model_answer_stage2: Revise: dropout rose only for program students, who work 25 hours a week, so the cause is work pressure.

opening_facts: A cosmetics brand launched a refillable lipstick. Sales of the lipstick are on plan, but refill sales are 70% below plan.
new_fact: Only 20% of stores stock the refills. In stores that stock them, refill sales per lipstick sold match plan.
model_answer_stage1: Buyers likely aren't coming back for refills because they can't find them in stores. I'd compare refill sales in stores that stock refills with those that don't.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: only 20% of stores stock refills, and where they do, refill sales match plan.

opening_facts: A city's pothole repairs now take 30 days on average, up from 10 last year.
new_fact: Crews fix as many potholes per day as last year, but reported potholes doubled after the city launched a phone app for reporting them.
model_answer_stage1: Repairs now take 30 days instead of 10, likely because crews are fixing fewer potholes per day. I'd compare repairs per crew per day with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: crews fix as many as before. Reports doubled after the new app, so the backlog grew.

opening_facts: A commercial cleaning company's cost per building cleaned rose 15% this year, while wage rates were flat.
new_fact: Hours spent inside each building are unchanged, but travel time between buildings doubled after the company won contracts spread over a wider area.
model_answer_stage1: With wage rates flat, the 15% rise in cost per building likely comes from crews spending more hours in each building. I'd compare hours on site per building with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: hours on site are unchanged. Travel between buildings doubled, so the cost is travel time.

opening_facts: A startup estimated 50,000 US households would buy its $3,000 home sauna in its first year. It sold 4,000.
new_fact: 30% of people who asked for a quote bought, above the 20% planned. But quote requests were 85% below plan, because most homes on the target list have no room for a sauna.
model_answer_stage1: Selling 4,000 saunas against 50,000 planned likely means the $3,000 price is too high for most households. I'd compare how many quotes turn into sales at different prices.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: 30% of quotes became sales, above plan, so price isn't it. Far fewer homes have room for one.

opening_facts: A regional ballet company's attendance fell 30% over two seasons.
new_fact: Ticket prices are unchanged, and subscribers renewed at the usual 85%. Single-ticket sales fell 50% after most performances moved from Saturday to weekday evenings, when the company lost its Saturday slot at the city theater.
model_answer_stage1: Attendance likely fell because the recent productions were less popular and casual audiences stayed away. I'd compare single-ticket sales by production.
model_answer_stage2: Revise: subscribers renewed as usual. Single-ticket sales halved after shows moved to weekdays, so it's the schedule.

opening_facts: A retailer replaced the lighting in its 30 stores with LEDs, expecting to cut store electricity use 30%. In the first year, use fell only 10%.
new_fact: Electricity used for lighting fell 55%, as planned. But lighting is only 20% of each store's electricity use; the plan assumed 55%.
model_answer_stage1: The LEDs are likely saving less than the supplier promised. I'd meter lighting use in a few stores before and after.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: lighting use fell 55% as planned. The plan assumed lighting was 55% of use, not 20%.

opening_facts: US sales of new upright pianos fell 40% over five years, while the number of children taking piano lessons was flat.
new_fact: Digital piano sales doubled over the same period, and 70% of beginners now start on a digital piano.
model_answer_stage1: With lessons flat, fewer new pianos likely means families are buying something else to play on, probably digital pianos. I'd compare digital and acoustic piano sales over the period.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: digital piano sales doubled, and 70% of beginners now start on one.

opening_facts: A private school's yearly deficit grew from $1M to $3M in two years, while enrollment was flat.
new_fact: Staff and building costs rose 3%, in line with plan. The tuition list price rose 4%, but the share of students on financial aid rose from 20% to 35%.
model_answer_stage1: With enrollment flat, the deficit likely grew because costs rose faster than tuition, probably staff pay. I'd compare staff costs per student with two years ago.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: staff and building costs rose only 3%. Aid recipients rose from 20% to 35%, so tuition collected fell.

opening_facts: A regional ice-cream maker's grocery sales grew 2% this year, while its category grew 10%.
new_fact: In its 400 long-time stores, its sales grew 9%, close to the category. It lost its place in a 150-store chain that now stocks only national brands and its own label.
model_answer_stage1: Sales likely lagged because the brand lost shelf space, probably at a big retailer. I'd split sales by retailer and compare stores that carry it this year and last.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: it grew 9% in its long-time stores and lost a 150-store chain.

opening_facts: An insurance brokerage bought a smaller brokerage, expecting to keep 90% of its clients. It kept 65%.
new_fact: Clients whose broker stayed renewed at 92%. But 12 of the 30 brokers at the acquired firm left within six months, and most of their clients followed them.
model_answer_stage1: Keeping 65% of clients instead of 90% likely means the buyer raised prices after the deal. I'd compare renewal rates before and after the deal, by client, and ask clients who left why.
model_answer_stage2: Revise: clients whose broker stayed renewed at 92%. The losses follow the 12 brokers who left.

opening_facts: A state's restaurant food-safety inspections fell 30% behind schedule in a year.
new_fact: Inspector headcount and time per inspection are unchanged, but inspectors now spend 30% of their working days driving after the agency closed 4 of its 10 regional offices.
model_answer_stage1: Inspections likely fell 30% behind because inspectors now spend more of their day traveling between restaurants. I'd compare inspector hours spent driving and inspecting with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: headcount and inspection time are unchanged, but driving now takes 30% of inspectors' days since offices closed.

opening_facts: A theme park's average ride wait rose from 20 to 35 minutes this season, while attendance was flat.
new_fact: Three of the park's 12 major rides were closed for repairs for most of the season. The rides that were open ran at normal capacity.
model_answer_stage1: With attendance flat, longer waits likely mean less ride capacity, perhaps rides closed or running slower. I'd check each ride's operating hours and riders per hour this season.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: three of 12 major rides were closed for most of the season, so the same crowds share fewer rides.

opening_facts: A carmaker launched an electric pickup. Orders beat plan, but 25% of buyers canceled before delivery.
new_fact: Cancellations rose sharply once delivery waits stretched from 3 to 9 months. Buyers who got their trucks within 3 months canceled at 3%.
model_answer_stage1: With orders beating plan, the 25% cancellation rate likely comes from buyers put off by reviews of the truck's range after ordering. I'd compare cancellations before and after the main reviews came out.
model_answer_stage2: Revise: cancellations track waiting time. Buyers who waited under 3 months canceled at 3%, so it's the 9-month wait.

opening_facts: An office-supply wholesaler lost 15% of its business customers in a year.
new_fact: Lost customers moved to an online marketplace that delivers the next day; the wholesaler delivers in 3 days. Prices at the two are within 2%.
model_answer_stage1: The 15% of customers lost likely left for a supplier that delivers faster. I'd ask lost customers who they switched to and why.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: lost customers moved to a next-day marketplace at prices within 2%, so speed, not price, drove them away.

opening_facts: A network of blood-testing labs saw profit fall 20% this year, while test volume rose 15%.
new_fact: Revenue per test is unchanged. Cost per test rose 15% because the network sends 30% of its tests to outside labs during a staff shortage.
model_answer_stage1: Profit fell despite more tests, likely because insurers are paying less per test. I'd compare payment per test by insurer with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: revenue per test is unchanged. Cost per test rose 15% from sending tests to outside labs.

opening_facts: A cloud-storage company's new business customers grew 40%, but spending by existing customers fell: net revenue retention dropped from 115% to 98%.
new_fact: Customers who adopted the new admin console kept expanding as before. 70% of customers never adopted it after it replaced the old console, and their spending fell.
model_answer_stage1: Retention fell from 115% to 98% while new customers grew 40%, so existing customers likely cut budgets in a weaker economy. I'd compare spending changes by customer industry and size.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: customers who adopted the new console kept expanding. The fall is among the 70% who never adopted it.

opening_facts: Ships at a container port now wait 4 days on average for a berth, up from 1 day, while ship arrivals rose 5%.
new_fact: Cranes work at normal speed, but containers sit in the yard 9 days instead of 4 because truckers can't get appointments to collect them, so the yard is full.
model_answer_stage1: With arrivals up only 5%, longer waits more likely come from slower unloading at the berth. I'd compare crane moves per hour with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: cranes work at normal speed. The yard is full because containers wait 9 days for pickup.

opening_facts: A city raised peak-hour road tolls 25% to cut congestion. Peak traffic fell only 3%.
new_fact: Most peak trips are commuters whose employers pay their tolls. Among drivers who pay their own tolls, peak trips fell 15%.
model_answer_stage1: Traffic barely fell, likely because commuters have no good alternative to driving at peak. I'd compare peak trips with transit use and work start times.
model_answer_stage2: Revise: drivers who pay their own tolls cut trips 15%. Most peak drivers don't pay, so the toll doesn't reach them.

opening_facts: A Korean bakery-café chain opened 30 cafés in the US. Average sales per café are half of plan.
new_fact: Cafés in neighborhoods with large Asian-American populations hit plan; the rest reached 30% of plan. Prices match local bakeries, and in a survey most other shoppers didn't know what the cafés sell.
model_answer_stage1: Sales are likely low because prices are too high for US shoppers. I'd compare prices and sales with nearby bakeries.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: prices match local bakeries. Cafés outside Asian-American neighborhoods sell far less, and shoppers there don't know what the cafés sell.

opening_facts: US sales of new motor homes fell 35% over two years, after record highs.
new_fact: Used motor-home listings tripled as owners who bought during the boom sold, and used prices fell 25%. Campground bookings are flat.
model_answer_stage1: Sales likely fell because people have lost interest in road trips since the boom. I'd compare campground bookings and road-trip surveys with two years ago.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: campground bookings are flat. Boom-era buyers are flooding the market with cheap used motor homes.

opening_facts: A national rail operator's on-time rate fell from 90% to 78% in a year.
new_fact: Delays from train faults are unchanged. 70% of the new delay minutes come from speed limits put on tracks after inspections found worn rails.
model_answer_stage1: Punctuality likely fell because aging trains break down more often. I'd compare delay minutes by cause with last year.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: train-fault delays are unchanged. Most new delays come from speed limits on worn track.

opening_facts: A chain of 80 daycare centers missed its profit plan by 30% in the year after it bought 15 more centers.
new_fact: Parent demand matches plan, with waitlists at most centers. But 15 centers bought last year run at 60% of their licensed capacity because they can't hire enough teachers to meet required ratios.
model_answer_stage1: Profit likely missed the plan by 30% because fewer families than planned are enrolling children at the newly bought centers. I'd compare enrollment and waitlists by center with plan.
model_answer_stage2: Drop: demand matches plan, with waitlists. Fifteen centers run at 60% of capacity because they can't hire teachers.
